page_title: Folderglass for Mac: Press Space, See Inside

sources.entry: Folderglass - Quick Look extension for folders: real size including subfolders, file-type breakdown, largest and newest files, git branch and status, and the README rendered inline. Also previews zip contents and Markdown. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/justadityaraj/folderglass) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.name: Folderglass
summary.one_liner: Folderglass is a free, open-source macOS Quick Look extension that shows a folder's real size including subfolders, file-type breakdown, largest and newest files, git branch and README when you press Space.
use_cases: check how big a folder is without Get Info or Terminal
find the largest files inside a project or downloads folder
see recently changed files across subfolders
check git branch and uncommitted changes from Finder
preview a README or Markdown file inline
browse zip archive contents without extracting
summary.what_it_does: Folderglass adds a Quick Look preview for folders on macOS: select a folder in Finder and press Space. It totals every file in every subfolder, shows the file count and when anything last changed, and displays a type bar for video, images, code, documents, archives and audio. Tabs list the 100 largest and 100 newest files with their subfolders, plus a sortable table of the top level. For git folders it reads the .git directory directly to show the branch, last commit, author and counts of modified or deleted tracked files, and renders the README. It also previews zip contents with uncompressed sizes and renders Markdown files offline. The extension is sandboxed and read-only.
notable: Reads .git directly to show branch, last commit and modified/deleted counts, including linked worktrees
Sandboxed, read-only Quick Look extension with no network access and no analytics
Installable via Homebrew (builds from source) or notarized DMG download
Huge folder counting stops after 15 seconds by default and the limit is configurable
caveats: Only one Quick Look extension per file type is active, so other folder preview extensions must be turned off in System Settings
Building from source via Homebrew or git clone needs Xcode Command Line Tools
Untracked files are not counted in git status
